description_full: InMode Ltd. designs, develops, manufactures, and markets minimally invasive aesthetic medical products based on its proprietary radio frequency assisted lipolysis and deep subdermal fractional radiofrequency technologies in the United States, Europe, Asia, and internationally. It offers minimally invasive aesthetic medical products for various procedures, such as liposuction with simultaneous skin tightening, body and face contouring, and ablative skin rejuvenation treatments, as well as for use in women's health conditions and procedures. The company also designs, develops, manufactures, and markets non-invasive medical aesthetic products that target an array of procedures, including permanent hair reduction, facial skin rejuvenation, wrinkle reduction, cellulite treatment, skin appearance and texture, and superficial benign vascular and pigmented lesions. In addition, it offers hands-free medical aesthetic products that target a range of procedures, such as skin tightening, fat reduction, and muscle stimulation. The company sells and markets its products in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Ireland, Spain, Portugal, France, Belgium, Luxemburg, Italy, Germany, Austria, Japan, Australia, and India through distributors. The company was formerly known as Invasix Ltd. and changed its name to InMode Ltd. in November 2017. The company was incorporated in 2008 and is headquartered in Yokne'am, Israel.

financial_summary: InMode Ltd. is a small-cap healthcare business with a $767M market cap on $370M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at -7% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome. Operating margins are contracting by -2.5pp, the first warning that competitive pressure is eroding the franchise.
Returns on capital run at 101% against a 11% cost of capital — a 90-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 84% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $84M in free cash flow — roughly 23 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.91× cash conversion.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 40× is fortress-like.

Management returns a meaningful 16.6% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 13% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 2.6× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
